samples.question: The upper part of this image shows an empty 5-by-5 grid. Beside each of its five rows a group of red dots is drawn, and under each of its five columns a group of blue dots is drawn. The number of red dots beside a row is the number of green cells that row must contain, and the number of blue dots under a column is the number of green cells that column must contain. Below are three filled 5-by-5 grids, labeled A, B and C from left to right, in which some cells are painted green. A candidate grid agrees with the tally when, for every one of the five rows, its number of green cells equals the number of red dots beside that row of the upper grid, and, for every one of the five columns, its number of green cells equals the number of blue dots under that column. Exactly one of A, B and C agrees with the tally. Each of the other two matches the red row dots only or the blue column dots only, never both, and all three candidates contain the same total number of green cells, so neither the row dots alone nor the column dots alone nor the total amount of green identifies the answer. Which candidate grid agrees with the tally? Answer A, B, or C.
